validation.reference_product: NASA HLS v2.0 (Landsat L30 + Sentinel-2 S30 surface reflectance)

selection.method: Maximum common cloud-free study-area coverage; ties favor closer dates. Detection agreement is not used for selection.

baseline.nisar_method: per-pixel median of preceding GCOV observations

comparison.qa_mask: HLS v2 Fmask: cloud, adjacent-to-cloud/shadow, cloud shadow, snow/ice, and high aerosol
comparison.optical_support_method: native HLS 30 m cells with area-averaged NISAR valid/candidate fractions

radar_grid_metrics.note: Legacy aligned radar-grid counts retained for reproducibility; finer radar pixels are not independent HLS samples.

optical_support.support: native HLS 30 m cells with area-averaged NISAR valid/candidate fractions
optical_support.resampling: area-weighted average from native GCOV grid to HLS grid

validation.reason: Too few co-registered, cloud-free pixels overlap the wetland mask for a useful check.
limitations: This is a cross-sensor agreement check, not field truth or a formal accuracy estimate.
HLS dates may differ from NISAR dates by the offsets shown; water can change between acquisitions.
Clouds and HLS's 30 m pixels reduce comparable coverage relative to the NISAR grid.
Pixels flagged with high aerosol optical thickness are excluded; lower aerosol levels can still affect reflectance.
MNDWI can miss flooded vegetation, turbid water, and mixed shoreline pixels.
S30/L30 bands are harmonized, but residual sensor and atmospheric differences can affect mixed-sensor pairs.
Only open-water candidates are evaluated; vegetated-inundation candidates are not validated.

comparison.optical_support_method: native HLS 30 m cells with area-averaged NISAR valid/candidate fractions

resampling_audit.method: Nearest-neighbour index resampling diagnostic, without changing the published bilinear comparison.

proximity_audit.note: Proximity is a diagnostic only; it does not change exact-match scores or demonstrate a registration error.

detector_audit.finding: The HH-darkening rule tests backscatter decrease only; it does not test whether a previously dry pixel became water.
detector_audit.existing_water_interpretation: Water on both optical dates supports a change over existing water rather than independently observed new inundation. The physical cause remains unknown.
detector_audit.quality_limitation: Radar quality screening for this run: finite positive HHHH/HVHV; GCOV numberOfLooks > 0 and metadata-declared fill exclusions where raw quality layers are present; optional external binary mask; GCOV averaging-ensemble mask recorded but not treated as validity.

limitations: Optical water on both dates is persistent over this pair, not proof of permanent water.
Radar darkening alone does not distinguish new water from changes in existing water or other scattering changes.
The optical image dates differ from radar dates; this audit cannot isolate the cause of disagreement.
HLS MNDWI is a simple reference rule, not an authoritative flood map or field truth.
Legacy radar-grid confusion counts are retained for reproducibility; native-HLS area-weighted scores use partial radar support per 30 m HLS cell.
No detector thresholds or results were tuned to the optical scores.
evidence.rgb_display: B04/B03/B02 surface reflectance, common 0–0.30 brightness scale and gamma 2.2. Clouds remain visible in RGB; grey water-mask pixels are excluded.
evidence.display_note: All panels share geographic extent. Continuous images use bilinear display resampling; categorical masks use nearest neighbour. Transparent pixels are outside the study mask. HLS source resolution is 30 m; radar-grid pixels are not independent optical samples. The report also includes an area-weighted score on native HLS cells.
